cd /home/mike/nexus-wt/gv4 && cat > docs/TELEMETRY.md <<'EOF'
# Telemetry: what Nexus records about a session, and where it goes

Nexus Code sends no telemetry. It has no analytics, crash-report or trace exporter, and nothing described on this page leaves the machine. The only requests Nexus makes are the ones you configure: your model provider, the MCP servers you add, and web tools when the agent uses them.

What Nexus does keep is a **local trace file** per session: timing records of turns, tool calls, model requests and context compactions, written to your home directory so that you can see where a session spent its time. This page says what is in that file, how to turn it off, and how long it is kept.

## Where it is

```
~/.local/share/nexus/traces/<session id>/trace.jsonl
```

One JSON object per line, in the OTLP/JSON file-exporter shape (`resourceSpans` → `scopeSpans` → `spans`), so standard OpenTelemetry tools can read it if you choose to load it into one. The directories are created with mode `0700` and the file with `0600`. Nexus refuses to write through a symbolic link or to a file with more than one name.

## What is in it

Each line is one finished span: a name, a start and end time, a random trace id and span id, a parent span id, a status (ok, error, unset) and the attributes below. The resource carries `service.name` (`nexus-code`) and the scope carries the Nexus version.

| Span | Attributes |
|---|---|
| `nexus.agent.turn` (one per turn) | `nexus.task.id`, `nexus.turn.execution`, `nexus.turn.outcome` |
| `nexus.agent.tool` (one per tool call) | `nexus.tool.name`, `nexus.tool.actor` (agent or subagent), `nexus.tool.step`, `nexus.tool.success`, `nexus.tool.duration_ms` |
| model request, named `<operation> <model>` | `gen_ai.operation.name`, `gen_ai.provider.name`, `gen_ai.request.model` |
| `nexus.context.compaction` | `nexus.compaction.trigger`, `nexus.compaction.step`, `nexus.compaction.before_tokens`, `nexus.compaction.after_tokens`, `nexus.compaction.pressure_only`, `nexus.compaction.archived_messages`, `nexus.compaction.durable`, `nexus.compaction.committed` |

What is **not** in it: prompts, model replies, tool arguments, tool output, file contents, file paths, commands, environment variables or credentials. The writer refuses the attribute names that would carry message content or the superseded GenAI names (`gen_ai.prompt`, `gen_ai.completion`, `gen_ai.input.messages`, `gen_ai.output.messages`, `gen_ai.system`, `gen_ai.usage.prompt_tokens`, `gen_ai.usage.completion_tokens`). Every span name and attribute value also passes through the same secret classifier that protects outbound requests, and a classified value is replaced irreversibly before the line is written.

A test (`cli/test/trace_transparency.test.ts`) fails when the client starts writing a span or attribute name that this table does not list.

## Turning it off

```sh
export NEXUS_TRACES=off      # also accepted: 0, false, no
```

With traces off, Nexus creates no trace file and no trace directory. Files written earlier stay until the retention period removes them or you delete them. A trace that cannot be written (a read-only home, a full disk) never interrupts a session either way.

## How long it is kept

Trace files older than **30 days** are removed. The check runs once when a session starts tracing; it removes a session's `trace.jsonl` when that file was last written more than the period ago, and the session's directory if that leaves it empty.

```sh
export NEXUS_TRACE_RETENTION_DAYS=7     # keep one week
export NEXUS_TRACE_RETENTION_DAYS=0     # keep indefinitely
```

A value that is not a whole number of days falls back to 30. Retention only ever removes a regular trace file inside a real session directory under `traces/`; it follows no links and touches nothing else. Before v1.3.0 trace files were kept indefinitely, so the first session after upgrading removes traces older than 30 days unless you set the variable to `0`.

To delete every trace now: `rm -r ~/.local/share/nexus/traces`.

## Other files Nexus keeps locally

These are session data, not telemetry, and have their own documentation: saved sessions and their exports, the flight recorder, verification attempts and evidence. They can contain your prompts and tool output, redacted by the same classifier; they also stay on the machine unless you export and share them.

## How this is checked

- The trace writer imports only file, path, crypto and OS modules; a test asserts that list.
- A test writes traces with the socket, HTTP, DNS, datagram and `fetch` entry points replaced by functions that fail, and asserts that none was called.
- Tests cover the off switch (nothing created) and retention (old files removed; links, hard links, foreign files and unknown directory names left alone).

This settles plan unit GV-4 and the earlier PC-5.

# Sidecar protocol schema

`sidecar-v1.schema.json` is the JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of the Nexus sidecar protocol, version 1: the newline-delimited JSON a client exchanges with the Node sidecar. `$defs.SidecarEvent` is every message the sidecar sends, `$defs.SidecarCommand` every message a client sends. Each is a `oneOf` over the message variants, told apart by the constant `type`; every message also carries `v`, the protocol version.

The file is generated from the types in `cli/src/protocol.ts` by the TypeScript type checker. Do not edit it by hand: change the types, then regenerate.

```bash
cd cli
node scripts/gen_protocol_schema.mjs           # rewrite docs/protocol/sidecar-v1.schema.json
node scripts/gen_protocol_schema.mjs --check   # exit 1 when the schema or the ledger is stale
```

`cli/test/protocol_schema.test.ts` runs the same comparison, so CI fails when a protocol type changes and the schema does not.

## Recording a version decision

`VERSIONS.json` is the version ledger: entries `{ "protocol", "schemaSha256", "note" }`, newest last. The newest entry must carry the SHA-256 of the checked-in schema and the current `PROTOCOL_VERSION`. A type change therefore needs two things: a regenerated schema and a new ledger entry whose `note` states the decision, either the same version because the change is additive and compatible (a new optional field, a new message an older peer ignores), or a bumped `PROTOCOL_VERSION`. Append entries; leave earlier ones as they are.

## Extra properties are allowed

No object in the schema sets `additionalProperties: false`. A newer sidecar may add an optional field to an event, and an older client must ignore it, so a schema that forbade unknown fields would reject messages the protocol means to accept. Commands are open for the same reason in the other direction: `parseCommand` reads the fields it knows and drops the rest. The schema checks what is required and the type of every field it names. `additionalProperties` appears only where a type has an index signature, where it gives the type of every value.

A tuple (`ReceiptRow`) is the exception: its length is fixed, as in the type.

## What the generator does with each type

- An interface or type alias declared under `cli/src` is written once under `$defs` and referenced with `$ref`. An instantiated generic (`Pick<SlashSpec, ...>`) and an intersection that forms a message (`models.catalog`) are written out in place.
- A union of string literals is an `enum`; `T | null` is `anyOf` with `{"type": "null"}`; an optional property is left out of `required`.
- JSDoc comments on types and properties become `description`.
- Definitions, properties, `required` lists, enum values and variants are sorted, so the output is the same on every run.
- A type with no JSON form (a function, an enum, a tuple with optional elements) stops the generator with an error naming the property.

You are implementing slice B of plan unit PF-1 (v1.3.0) in the nexus-code repository: capability negotiation for the sidecar client protocol. Work ONLY in the git worktree `/home/mike/nexus-wt/pf1b` (branch `v1/pf1b-capability-negotiation`, stacked on slice A, which published the protocol schema). Read `/home/mike/nexus-wt/pf1b/AGENTS.md` and `/home/mike/nexus-wt/pf1b/docs/protocol/README.md` first.

## Context
- The sidecar protocol is NDJSON over stdio between a client (the Rust TUI in `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/`) and the Node sidecar (`cli/src/sidecar.ts`). Types and the parser are in `cli/src/protocol.ts` (`PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1`, `SidecarEvent`, `SidecarCommand`, `parseCommand`, `encodeEvent`). The Rust mirror is `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/protocol.rs`; the client checks the version in `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/live_state.rs` (`Event::Hello { protocol, commands } if protocol == PROTOCOL_VERSION`).
- Today negotiation is one-way: the sidecar emits `hello { protocol: 1, pid, commands }` at start and the client either matches exactly or fails.
- Slice A added a GENERATED schema `docs/protocol/sidecar-v1.schema.json` (generator `cli/scripts/gen_protocol_schema.mjs`), a ledger `docs/protocol/VERSIONS.json`, and `cli/test/protocol_schema.test.ts`, which fails when a protocol type changes without a regenerated schema and a new ledger entry. A golden corpus `cli/test/fixtures/protocol_v1_golden.jsonl` is shared with a Rust test (`golden_protocol_v1_corpus` in protocol.rs).
- Plan text (docs/v1.3.0/PLAN.md): PF-1 "capability negotiation in `hello` / `initialize` (version range, `experimental` flag)"; principle 8 "Experimental is a flag. New methods sit behind `experimental` at `initialize` until a conformance suite has run against two real clients"; risk row "Protocol churn after publication: `experimental` flag, version range in `hello`, schema diff in CI".

## Design to implement (additive; the protocol version stays 1)
1. `hello` event gains OPTIONAL fields (older clients ignore them):
   - `protocol_min: number`, `protocol_max: number`: the inclusive range of protocol versions this sidecar can speak (both 1 today). `protocol` stays and keeps its meaning (the version the sidecar speaks by default).
   - `capabilities: string[]`: stable feature names the sidecar supports. Derive the list from one exported constant in `cli/src/protocol.ts` (for example the command types a client may send that are beyond the minimal set: `steer`, `answer`, `checkpoint.choice`, `tool.detail`, `receipt`, `models.list`, `model.select`, `provider.connect`, `provider.disconnect`, `slash`). Choose names deliberately, document each in a JSDoc comment, keep the list sorted.
   - `experimental: string[]`: names of experimental features this sidecar offers (empty today; the mechanism must exist and be tested with a test-only registration or an injectable list, NOT by inventing a fake product feature).
2. New command `initialize`: `{ type: "initialize", id, client: { name: string, version: string }, protocol_min?: number, protocol_max?: number, experimental?: boolean }`. Validation in `parseCommand` (bounded string lengths, integers in a sane range, min <= max).
3. New event `initialized`: `{ type: "initialized", id, protocol: number, capabilities: string[], experimental: string[] }`, sent in answer to `initialize`. `protocol` is the highest version in the overlap of the two ranges; `experimental` lists the experimental features now enabled for this connection (empty unless the client asked with `experimental: true`).
4. No overlap between the client's range and the sidecar's: answer with the existing `error` event carrying a NEW error code `UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL` and a message naming both ranges. Do not crash and do not close the connection.
5. `initialize` is OPTIONAL. A client that never sends it gets exactly today's behaviour. A second `initialize` on the same connection is refused with `BAD_REQUEST` (state the rule in a comment). `initialize` while a turn is running is fine (it only records connection state).
6. An experimental feature used without having been enabled is refused with a NEW error code `EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLED`. Provide the gate as a small function in the sidecar that later slices call (for example `requireExperimental(name, id)`), and test it through a test-only path.
7. `parseCommand` today throws on `msg.v !== PROTOCOL_VERSION`. Make it accept any `v` inside the sidecar's supported range (still just 1), with the range in one exported constant pair so a future version bump changes one place.
8. Rust client (`protocol.rs`, `live_state.rs`): parse the new optional `hello` fields with `#[serde(default)]`; decide compatibility by range overlap when `protocol_min`/`protocol_max` are present (the client supports exactly `PROTOCOL_VERSION` today, expressed as a min and max constant), and by exact match when they are absent (an older sidecar). Keep the existing failure message style, and name both ranges in it. Add the `Initialized` event variant so the client does not treat it as unknown; the TUI does NOT need to send `initialize` in this slice (say so in a comment). Check how unknown event types are handled today and do not change that.
9. Regenerate the schema (`cd cli && node scripts/gen_protocol_schema.mjs`) and APPEND a ledger entry to `docs/protocol/VERSIONS.json` with the new hash, `"protocol": 1`, and a note saying the change is additive and why the version does not move. Do not edit the earlier entry.
10. Add records for `initialize` and `initialized`, and a `hello` WITH the new fields, to the golden corpus, and make both the TS golden test and the Rust `golden_protocol_v1_corpus` test cover them (read that Rust test to see how it dispatches on names and directions; extend it the same way). Do not remove or alter existing corpus records.

## Constraints (hard)
- Backward compatible both ways: an old client against the new sidecar, and the new client against an old sidecar (no new fields), must behave as before. Write a test for each direction.
- No new dependency (npm or cargo). `cli/package.json`, the npm lockfile, `core/Cargo.toml` and `core/Cargo.lock` must not change.
- Preserve existing comments and unrelated code. Touch only: `cli/src/protocol.ts`, `cli/src/sidecar.ts`, `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/protocol.rs`, `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/live_state.rs`, the generated schema, the ledger, the golden corpus, and test files. If you believe another file must change, STOP and tell me which and why (several source files are claimed by other agents; in particular do not edit `cli/src/index.ts`, `cli/src/agent.ts`, `cli/src/config.ts`, `core/src/bin/nexus_tui/live_view.rs`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/USER_MANUAL.md`).
- Do not run `git commit`, `git push`, `gh`, or anything that publishes. Leave changes uncommitted for my review.
- Foreground only: no background jobs, no watcher or polling loops, never `pkill -f`. Never read or print `~/.config/nexus/config.env`. No network calls except the local XERJ query below.
- TypeScript tests: `cd /home/mike/nexus-wt/pf1b/cli && HOME=$(mktemp -d) node --import tsx --test test/<name>.test.ts` (throwaway HOME is mandatory). `cli/node_modules` is already copied in. Type-check with `npx tsc --noEmit`. Built Rust binaries from the BASE tree are in `core/target/release/`; after you change Rust code, rebuild so the TS tests that spawn the TUI or core use your code.
- Rust: always `export CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/mike/nexus-wt/pf1b/core/target` first. Build with `cargo build --release --locked --bin harness-core --bin nexus-tui`; run the TUI protocol tests with `cargo test --locked --bin nexus-tui protocol` and the live_state tests with `cargo test --locked --bin nexus-tui live_state` (adjust filters after reading the test module names); run `cargo clippy --locked --bin nexus-tui` and fix what your change introduces. Check formatting the way the repo does (`scripts/check_fmt.sh` or `cargo fmt --check`; read the script first).
- Reference coding (required by AGENTS.md): before writing, run a short query against the local XERJ node for how a peer does protocol initialize / capability negotiation, for example `xerj code opencode "initialize capabilities protocolVersion experimental" -k 4 --full 400` and `xerj search --prefix xc-opencode "acp initialize protocolVersion clientCapabilities" -k 4`. The opencode index is flagged "not verified complete". Record in your report what you saw, what you took, what you rejected. Reference code is read-only inspiration; copy nothing verbatim.

## Tests to write (at minimum)
- `parseCommand`: valid `initialize`; each invalid shape rejected with a clear message (missing client, non-string name, oversized strings, non-integer or negative range, min > max); `v` inside the range accepted and outside rejected.
- Sidecar behaviour (extend `cli/test/sidecar.test.ts` or add `cli/test/sidecar_initialize.test.ts`, following how existing sidecar tests drive `handleLine` and collect emitted events): `hello` carries the range, capabilities (equal to the exported constant, sorted) and `experimental`; `initialize` with an overlapping range answers `initialized` with the chosen version; a non-overlapping range answers `error` / `UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL` naming both ranges and the sidecar keeps serving later commands; a second `initialize` is `BAD_REQUEST`; no `initialize` at all leaves every existing sidecar test passing unchanged; the experimental gate refuses with `EXPERIMENTAL_DISABLED` until `initialize` asked for experimental, then allows.
- Rust: `hello` with and without the new fields parses; range overlap accepted; a sidecar whose range excludes the client's version fails with the message naming both ranges; an older sidecar with a different exact `protocol` still fails as before; `initialized` parses; the golden corpus test covers the new records.
- `protocol_schema.test.ts` must pass with the regenerated schema and the appended ledger entry, and its "every `case` in parseCommand is a command variant" check must include `initialize`.

## Verify before reporting
`npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `protocol`, `protocol_golden`, `protocol_schema`, `sidecar` and every sidecar_* test file pass; `node scripts/check_test_leaks.mjs` passes; the Rust tests, clippy and format check pass; `git status --short` lists only files in the allowed set; `git diff --stat cli/package.json cli/package-lock.json core/Cargo.toml core/Cargo.lock` is empty.

## Report back (concise, facts only)
Files changed; the final shapes of `hello`, `initialize`, `initialized` and the two new error codes; the capability names you chose and why; exact test commands run with pass/fail counts (TS and Rust); the reference-coding record; anything you could not do or decided differently from this brief, and anything I should review. Do not claim something works unless you ran it.

content.text:
v1.3.0 is under way, with four units in flight on `release/v1.3.0`. Nothing is merged yet; three PRs are waiting on CI.

## In flight
- **PF-1, slice A (PR #697):** the client protocol is now published as a JSON Schema generated from the TypeScript types, checked in, with a test that fails when a type changes without a regenerated schema and a recorded version decision. I reran its tests myself after the subagent finished.
- **PF-1, slice B:** capability negotiation (a version range and an `experimental` flag in `hello`, plus an optional `initialize` exchange) is with a subagent now, covering both the TypeScript sidecar and the Rust client.
- **GV-4 (PR #695):** `NEXUS_TRACES=off` turns local traces off, trace files are pruned after 30 days by default, and `docs/TELEMETRY.md` lists everything the traces hold. A test asserts the trace writer makes no network call.
- **GV-3, part 1 (PR #696):** flight records and verification-file edit attempts are hash-chained, so an edited, removed or reordered record is reported with its position.

## Blocked by another lane's claims
- **PF-2 and VR-1** both need `cli/src/index.ts`, which Codex's tool-budget lane (PR #689) holds, along with the user manual and `config.ts`.
- **GV-3, part 2** needs the same file (to print the chain verdict in `nexus replay`) and `objective.ts`.

## Needs your attention
PR #689 keeps being pointed back at `main`. I retargeted it to `release/v1.3.0` twice, and the other session reset it to `main` both times, once after a force-push. It is at `main` again now. I've stopped moving it, since repeating that isn't working. If it merges into `main` it breaks your rule. Telling that session directly, or protecting `main` in GitHub settings, would settle it.

## Decisions I'm taking by default
- **GV-4 retention:** traces used to be kept forever. They are now removed after 30 days unless `NEXUS_TRACE_RETENTION_DAYS=0`. Say if you want a different default.
- **GV-3 limit:** a hash chain cannot show records cut from the end of a log. A flight reports that case as "not closed", and the stronger answer is the signed audit export (GV-2).
- **Changelog:** `CHANGELOG.md` is claimed by another lane, so I'm collecting v1.3.0 entries for release preparation instead of adding them per PR.

While the blocked units wait, I'm scoping the Cloudflare contest removal next.

# Nexus sidecar protocol

This is the reference for writing a client of the Nexus sidecar: the process that runs the agent and reports what it does. The Nexus terminal UI is one such client. The protocol is version 1.

The machine-readable form is [`protocol/sidecar-v1.schema.json`](protocol/sidecar-v1.schema.json), a JSON Schema generated from the types in `cli/src/protocol.ts`. This page says what the schema cannot: order, meaning and the rules of compatibility. Where the 

## What the protocol covers, and what it does not

A client starts the sidecar as a child process and talks to it over the child's standard input and output. That is the only transport.

Not part of this protocol today:

- No socket or network transport. A client cannot attach to a sidecar that another process started (planned as PF-3).
- No library entry point. The sidecar is a process, not an importable API (planned as PF-4).
- No Agent Client Protocol (ACP). This is Nexus's own protocol (ACP is planned as AC-1).

The sidecar projects the agent's state. It never asks the client to decide an outcome: whether a turn succeeded, whether a change is verified and whether a tool call is allowed are decided in the sidecar and reported. The one thing a client is asked for is a h

## Transport and framing

- The sidecar is the Node program `cli/dist/sidecar.js` (in an installed release, `lib/cli/dist/sidecar.js` under the Nexus home). Run it with `--help` for its options: endpoint, model, workspace, approval mode, `--resume`.
- The client writes commands to the sidecar's stdin and reads events from its stdout. Stdout carries protocol lines only. Stderr carries diagnostics for a log, in no fixed format.
- Each message is one JSON object on one line, UTF-8, ended by `\n` (newline-delimited JSON). A newline inside a string is escaped, as JSON requires. The sidecar ignores blank lines and accepts `\r\n`.
- Every message, in both directions, carries `v` (the protocol version, an integer) and `type` (a string that names the message).

I found two things on re-reading the shared log, one of them my own miss.

## I missed a reassignment
- **What happened:** at 02:35 UTC the other session (Codex) took over PF-1 and its files, recorded as "at owner direction", and at 02:47 it took the remaining GV-3 work.
- **My error:** I didn't re-read the claims before continuing, so I kept working on PF-1 for about 85 minutes after it was no longer mine.
- **What I did in that time:** committed and pushed slice B to its branch, then had a subagent build the last PF-1 slices on top of it.
- **Was anything of Codex's overwritten:** no. Codex rebased the slice B branch after my last push, and I haven't pushed to it since. PR #700 is its version, with one extra fix of its own.
- **The stranded work:** my slices C and D (protocol docs, the TypeScript/Rust parity tests, recorded-session replay) are complete and tested, but sit on a branch based on the pre-rebase commits. I've handed that branch over in the log, with what it contains and how to rebase it, and I won't open a PR for it or touch PF-1 files again unless it's handed back.

## `main` received v1.3.0 work
PR #689 (the tool-budget change) was merged into `main` at 02:31 UTC by the other session. `main` is now four commits and 14 files ahead of `release/v1.3.0`, which is what your rule was meant to prevent. Codex has since opened #699 to bring the same change onto the release branch. Nothing else has gone into `main`.

## Who has what now
- **Codex:**
  - PF-1 (#700).
  - A hash-chain follow-up to my GV-3 work (#701).
  - The README and quickstart contest-link cleanup I had deferred (#702).
  - A review-fixes PR (#703).
  - The budget port (#699).
- **Mine:** the doctor fix (#704, in CI).
- **Merged on the release branch so far:** GV-4, GV-3 part 1, PF-1 slice A and the Cloudflare removal, all from me.

## Next for me
PF-2 (versioning `nexus run --json` and documenting exit codes) is second in your priority order, and the file claims that blocked it are released. It edits `cli/src/index.ts` and the user manual, which #699 also changes. I'll start it once #699 lands so the two don't conflict, and check the claims again before I do.

If you'd rather I take different units so the two sessions stop overlapping, tell me which.

## Files

**Changed**
- `cli/scripts/gen_protocol_schema.mjs`: the two-keyword edit only.
- `cli/src/index.ts`: +21/−10, all inside the `run` command plus one import.
- `docs/USER_MANUAL.md`: +37, one block before "Viewing Tool Audit Logs".
- `docs/protocol/README.md`: +12, one section appended.

**Added**
- `cli/src/run_contract.ts`
- `cli/scripts/gen_run_result_schema.mjs`
- `cli/test/run_json_contract.test.ts`
- `docs/protocol/run-result-v1.schema.json`
- `docs/protocol/RUN_RESULT_VERSIONS.json`

`cli/src/core/app.ts` is not changed: `schema_version` is added where the document is printed (`runJsonResult` in `run_contract.ts`), so `runTask`'s return value is untouched. This differs from the original brief's "beside `TaskExecutionResult`" and follows your decision 2.

## Diff for the other agent

```
-class SchemaBuilder {
+export class SchemaBuilder {
-function sortKeys(object) {
+export function sortKeys(object) {
```

After it, `node scripts/gen_protocol_schema.mjs --check` passes and `sidecar-v1.schema.json` and `VERSIONS.json` have no diff.

## Result shape and versioning

- **Result (`RunJsonResult`):** `schema_version` first, then `taskId`, `success`, `status`, `prompt`, `output`, `plan`, `milestones`, `candidateId?`, `candidateIdentity?`, `validationReceipts`, `worktreeBinding?`, `tokenStats`, `durationMs`, `error?`, `logs?`, `turn`, `exitCode`, `evaluationToolReceipts?`, `cloudUsage?` (typed as `UsageTotals`).
- **Error document (`RunJsonError`):** `schema_version` first, then `taskId`, `success` (false), `status` ("failed"), `prompt`, `output`, `plan`, `milestones`, `validationReceipts`, `tokenStats`, `durationMs`, `error`.
- **Discrimination:** no discriminator member was added. Only a result has `turn` and `exitCode`; the schema root is `anyOf` over the two.
- **Rule:** an added optional member keeps the version; a removed or renamed member, or a changed type or meaning, bumps it. Constant: `RUN_RESULT_SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`.
- **Stream-json:** its `result` event now carries `schema_version` too; its `error` event is unchanged and documented as a different shape.

## Exit-code table (`RUN_EXIT_CODES`)

| Code | Name | When |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `ok` | `VERIFIED` or `NOT_REQUIRED` |
| 1 | `failed` | failed, blocked, limit reached, completed without a result, or a thrown error |
| 1 | `missing_prompt` | no task, no resume, terminal on stdin |
| 1 | `option_parse` | unknown option or missing option value |
| 2 | `unverified` | `UNVERIFIED` or `REGRESSION_FREE` |
| 2 | `usage` | invalid option or invalid task input before the run |
| 2 | `resume_unavailable` | no task to resume, or the fork failed |
| 2 | `task_not_found` | `--resume <id>` with no saved state |
| 130 | `interrupted` | SIGINT |

All literal exit codes in the `run` command now come from this table; no value changed. `index.ts` still exits with `result.exitCode` from `exitCodeForTurn`, and a test pins that function to the table for every execution × outcome pair, with the enums read from the generated schema.

**Findings (documented as they behave, not changed):**
- Code 2 has four meanings and code 1 has three; the manual says a consumer must read the document to tell them apart.
- The option parser exits 1 for an unknown option or a missing option value (observed by running `run --nope` and `run --input-json`). I added the `option_parse` row for it, which nobody asked for.
- `nexus run` with no task and an empty non-terminal stdin (for example `</dev/null`) now exits 2 with "no task: stdin was empty"; before it exited 1 with "missing required argument 'prompt'". This follows your decision 8; the old path is reached only with a terminal on stdin.
- `nexus run` with no task and a stdin pipe that is never closed now waits for it. The manual says so.
- `runTask` with `json` or `quiet` captures `process.stdout`, which silently drops node:test reports of tests that finished just before it in the same file. My in-process test is therefore first in the file, with a comment. `context_capacity_runtask.test.ts` uses the same `quiet` pattern and reports "tests 1", so it may be losing reports the same way; I did not investigate it.
- The schema is about 52 KB because it covers every type the result reaches (`TurnResult`, `ValidationReceipt` and others). Any change to those types now needs a regenerated schema and a ledger entry.

## Input contract

- **`--input-json <file|->`:** reads `{ "schema_version": 1, "task": "<text>" }`. It must be a JSON object, `schema_version` exactly 1, `task` a non-empty string (trimmed).
- **Authority:** only `task` is read. I mapped no other member onto options.
- **Plain stdin:** read as the task only when there is no argument, no `--input-json`, no `--resume` or `--fork-session`, and stdin is not a terminal.
- **Bounds:** 1,048,576 bytes and valid UTF-8; larger input is rejected, not truncated.
- **Usage errors (exit 2):** argument plus `--input-json`, an invalid document, an unreadable file, or empty stdin. The message goes to stderr and stdout stays empty.
- **With `--resume`:** `--input-json` is allowed and supplies the prompt, as an argument does today.

## Generator reuse

`gen_run_result_schema.mjs` imports `SchemaBuilder`, `sortKeys` and `sha256` from `gen_protocol_schema.mjs`. It repeats the checker-opening block and has its own ledger rule (`runResultLedgerProblem`, key `schema_version`).

## Verification

- **New tests:** `HOME=$(mktemp -d) node --import tsx --test test/run_json_contract.test.ts` gave 15/15, three times.
- **Coverage:** the consumer tests cover verified (0), `UNVERIFIED` and `REGRESSION_FREE` (2), `NOT_REQUIRED` (0), an inference failure (1), the error document (2), and the stream-json `result` event. The usage-error test has 15 cases.
- **Forbidden members:** a document with `yes`, `mode`, `workspace`, `endpoint` and others produces the same blocked run as without them and writes nothing.
- **Existing files, all passing:**

  | File | Passed |
  |---|---|
  | `protocol_schema` | 7/7 |
  | `protocol` | 10/10 |
  | `run_json_output` | 3/3 |
  | `stream_json` | 4/4 |
  | `context_capacity_runtask` | 1/1 |
  | `app` | 7/7 |
  | `step_loop` | 18/18 |
  | `suspend_resume_acceptance` | 3/3 |
  | `session_durable_fields` | 4/4 |
  | `cli_option_precedence` | 7/7 |
  | `durable_continuity` | 42/42 |

- **Scripts:** `check_test_leaks.mjs`, `check_doc_versions.mjs` and `check_requirements.mjs` (report mode) exit 0; both generators' `--check` pass.
- **Untouched:** the four manifest and lock files have no diff, and `git status --short` lists only the nine files above.
- **Drift demonstration:** with `driftDemo?: string` added to `TaskExecutionResult`, `--check` exited 1 and the schema test failed with "schema is out of date". I restored `app.ts` from a scratch copy; `git diff --stat cli/src/core/app.ts` is empty.
- **Compatibility diff:** the same scripted run (write a file with `-y`, exit 2) before and after, with ids, times, paths and numbers of two or more digits normalised, differs by exactly:
  ```
  2a3
  >   "schema_version": 1,
  ```
  "Before" came from a temporary copy of `HEAD:cli/src/index.ts` at `cli/src/pf2_base_index_tmp.ts`, deleted afterwards; no stash was used.

## Reference coding

One XERJ query: `xerj code opencode "run json output schema version exit code stdin prompt" -k 4 --full 400`. The index was flagged "not verified complete" and is 21 days old. The four hits (an MCP test server, a TUI `RunInput` type, an SSH registration parser, a session test helper) were not relevant. Nothing was taken or copied; the design follows the repo's own protocol-schema pattern.

## For your review

- One of my test loops ran past the tool's time limit and was moved to the background automatically. It finished with exit 0; I re-ran the three files it had not yet reported in the foreground.
- `docs/STREAM_JSON.md` still describes the `result` event without `schema_version`; it is outside my allowed files.
- `CHANGELOG.md` has no entry, as instructed.</result>

Ask the `run_turn.ts` owner to adopt it later. |

The duplication is real (the ladder and the type-check evidence mapping). Mitigate with parity tests. Do not construct a headless agent to avoid it: that drags in the bridge, the session and the model client.

## 3. CLI contract

```
nexus verify [--worktree <path> | -w <path>] [--base <ref>] [--head <ref>]
             [--verifier <cmd>] [--deliverable-file <path>]... [-y|--yes | --approve-verifier <sha256>]
             [--approve-verification-edit <path>]... [--review] [--objective <text>|--objective-file <f>]
             [--timeout-secs <n>] [--receipt <file>] [-j|--json]
```

- **Modes.** `--worktree` alone verifies the working tree against `HEAD`, or against `--base`. `--base` with `--head` verifies two commits. In both cases both trees are materialised into scratch directories so the caller's checkout is never written.
- **Why scratch directories.** `prepareBaselineTestsCopy` writes under `<workspace>/.nexus/verify/` (`independent_check.ts:785`). Run it on the scratch head, not the user's tree.
- **Verifier selection.** `--verifier` gives source `configured`. Otherwise discover from the base tree, never the head. A discovered verifier needs `-y` or `--approve-verifier <digest>` (the `describeVerifier` digest); otherwise the verdict is BLOCKED with the command and digest printed. This mirrors headless review mode (`spine_handlers.ts:201-203`).
- **Reviewer.** Off by default. `--review` requires a configured model and an objective; with no model the verdict is BLOCKED (`review_unavailable`). Without `--review` the receipt records `review: NOT_RUN`.

**Verdict rules** (computed outcome, then mapped; the reviewer and guard can only lower):

| Verdict | When | Exit |
|---|---|---|
| VERIFIED | Outcome `VERIFIED`: passed, tests executed, definition bound, deliverable-bound, and configured or independent. No unapproved guard finding. With `--review`, the reviewer said ACCEPT. | 0 `ok` |
| REGRESSION_FREE | Outcome `REGRESSION_FREE` | 2 `unverified` |
| UNVERIFIED | No applicable verifier, zero tests executed, or an empty diff (`NOTHING_TO_VERIFY`) | 2 `unverified` |
| UNVERIFIED | Outcome `NOT_ESTABLISHED`: verifier or enforced type-check failed or timed out; or the reviewer said REJECT | 1 `failed` |
| BLOCKED | Verifier not approved; an unapproved verification-config edit or detected weakening under mode `approve` or `block`; an untrusted checkout (`trustedGitArgs` throws); `--review` without a model; incomplete scan bounds | 3 `blocked` (new) |
| usage or bad ref | | 2 `usage` |
| SIGINT | | 130 |

Differences from `RUN_EXIT_CODES` (`cli/src/run_contract.ts:69`):
- Code 3 is new and collides with nothing. In `run`, BLOCKED is folded into 1; a CI gate needs "a human must decide" to be distinguishable from "tests failed".
- An empty diff is not 0. `run` gives `NOT_REQUIRED` → 0, but here the caller chooses the base.

**JSON.** `VerifyJsonOutput = VerifyJsonResult | VerifyJsonError` in a new `cli/src/verify_contract.ts`, with these members:
- `schema_version: 1` first.
- `verdict`, `outcome` (`EngineeringOutcome`), `reason`, `detail`, `exitCode`.
- `base` and `head` as `{ref, commit, tree}`.
- `verification: VerificationEvidence` (reused, includes `typecheck`), and a `baseline` summary.
- `guard: {mode, policySource, findings[{path, class, kind, weakening?, approved}], complete}`.
- `review: {status: "NOT_RUN" | "ACCEPT" | "REJECT", verdict?}`.
- `receipt: ValidationReceipt`.
- `environment` (names of the verdict-affecting variables that were set).
- `durationMs`.

Also add a `VERIFY_EXIT_CODES` table with the same shape as `RunExitCode`.

**Schema.** Generalise `cli/scripts/gen_run_result_schema.mjs` into a parameterised generator (root type, source file, version constant, ledger), or add a sibling `gen_verify_result_schema.mjs` reusing `SchemaBuilder`. Outputs are `docs/protocol/verify-result-v1.schema.json` and `VERIFY_RESULT_VERSIONS.json`. Tests mirror `cli/test/run_json_contract.test.ts:86-160`.

## 4. Security analysis for G-3

**Trust model to document.** The process launcher (argv and env) is the operator. The repository content, especially the head, is untrusted. VR-1 cannot defend against a hostile launcher; it can make every verdict-affecting input visible in the receipt. So structure the core as `verifyChange(request, operatorContext)`, with the request limited to worktree, base and head, so VR-2 can expose only the request.

| Attack | Existing protection | VR-1 must add |
|---|---|---|
| Head redefines the verifier (`package.json` test script, Makefile, conftest) | `snapshotVerifierDefinition` and `verifierDefinitionChangedSince` (`independent_check.ts:183, 601`); the agent refuses at `spine_handlers.ts:140-168` | Discover and bind from base; a definition change is never VERIFIED and is a guard finding |
| `--verifier 'echo ok'` or fabricated output | `hasExecutedTests` (zero tests → UNVERIFIED); deliverable binding by imports in pre-existing tests, not by output text (`tester.ts:1785-1790`); inline programs are unbindable (`independent_check.ts:106`) | Record the verifier source and digest in the receipt. Residual risk: a launcher-supplied script that prints a fake runner summary |

VR-1 is planned and its first slice is being built. PF-2 (#705) is still in CI.

## How `nexus verify` will work
The planning pass found it can be a thin command over functions that already exist, with no change to the large agent file another lane holds.

- **What it does:** given a base and a head, or a working tree, it runs the project's verifier on both and prints a verdict with a receipt.
- **Verdicts and exit codes:**

  | Verdict | Meaning | Exit |
  |---|---|---|
  | `VERIFIED` | tests that failed on the base now pass on the head, under the base's own test definition | 0 |
  | `REGRESSION_FREE` or `UNVERIFIED` | passed, but not provably tied to the change; or nothing to verify | 2 |
  | `UNVERIFIED` | the verifier failed or timed out | 1 |
  | `BLOCKED` | a human must decide, such as an unapproved verifier | 3 |

- **Code 3 is new.** A CI gate needs to tell "a human must decide" from "tests failed", and `nexus run` folds both into 1.
- **The caller's checkout is never written.** Both trees are copied into scratch directories.
- **The verifier is discovered from the base, never the head,** so a change can't redefine its own test command. A weakened or deleted test can't reach `VERIFIED`, because the base's tests are run against the head's code.

## Limits, which will be in the manual
- `VERIFIED` is not a statement of correctness. Without declared deliverable files the best verdict is `REGRESSION_FREE`.
- The repository's test code runs with the caller's privileges until a sandbox option is added in a later slice.
- A verifier command supplied by whoever launches the command, and written to print a fake test summary, can't be detected. The receipt records the command and its source so that's visible.

## Slices
1. Core and CLI, no model (in progress with a subagent).
2. Type-check evidence, verification-file findings, and the generated JSON schema.
3. A GitHub Action, a hostile-caller test suite, and the sandbox option.
4. The optional independent reviewer, which needs a model.

The full plan is saved at `/home/mike/nexus-wt/_plans/VR1_PLAN.md`.

PR #700's conflicts are resolved and pushed. It is mergeable again and its checks are rerunning.

## #700
- **Cause:** the release branch had published a newer protocol schema entry (from the tool-budget change) and added a golden test, and both collided with #700.
- **Resolution:** a merge commit of `release/v1.3.0` into the branch, with no rebase and no force-push. I kept both tests, put the already-published ledger entry ahead of #700's, and regenerated the schema from the merged types.
- **Checked locally:** all 404 Rust TUI tests pass, clippy and the format gate are clean, and the eight protocol, sidecar and budget suites pass.
- **Ownership:** PF-1 stays with Codex. I logged what I did and that you asked for it, and left the merge to that session once the checks are green.

One host note: clippy first crashed with a compiler panic from a corrupted incremental cache in that worktree. Deleting the cache directory fixed it; it wasn't a code problem.

## #705 (PF-2)
One of its three required checks failed, on a single test: `tui_diff_e2e`, a real-terminal resize test. The other two checks passed that same test at the same commit, and PF-2 changes nothing the terminal UI loads. I've rerun the failed job once to see if it repeats. If it does, I'll investigate instead of rerunning again.

## Also
- Codex's review-fixes PR (#703) merged into the release branch.
- VR-1's first slice is still with the subagent.

A watch is on #700 and #705.

<result>Slice 1 of VR-1 is implemented and uncommitted in `/home/mike/nexus-wt/vr1`. `tsc` is clean and all the checks you listed pass, but there are five places where the code forced a result the plan did not expect, listed below.

## Files
Added:
- `cli/src/core/verification_outcome.ts`
- `cli/src/core/verify.ts`
- `cli/src/verify_contract.ts`
- `cli/test/verification_outcome.test.ts`
- `cli/test/verify_command.test.ts`

Edited:
- `cli/src/index.ts`: two import lines and one contiguous `verify` block after `run`.
- `docs/USER_MANUAL.md`: one `### nexus verify` section, with an `#### Exit codes of nexus verify` subsection.

No helper files were needed. The brief says "three new test files"; it names two, and two exist (the contract-table tests are in `verify_command.test.ts`).

## Where the code disagreed with the plan
1. **A fix without `--deliverable-file` is not REGRESSION_FREE.** The plan expected REGRESSION_FREE (`tester.ts:1758`). On the plan's fixture, `snapshotVerifierDefinition` (`addTestSupportDependencies`, `independent_check.ts:284`) binds `src/math.js` as test support, because it is neither a declared deliverable nor in the package's runtime graph. The fix then counts as a verifier-definition change, so the result is UNVERIFIED / `VERIFIER_DEFINITION_CHANGED`, exit 1. With `"main"` pointing at the file it would be REGRESSION_FREE, as in PF-2's fixture. I did not work around it; the test asserts only "not VERIFIED".
2. **The ladder's reason is replaced in one case.** When the definition changed, the agent builds FAILED evidence without running the verifier, and the ladder says `VERIFIER_FAILED`. `verify` keeps the outcome (NOT_ESTABLISHED, exit 1) but reports `VERIFIER_DEFINITION_CHANGED` or `VERIFIER_DEFINITION_NOT_CAPTURED`, because the verifier never ran on the head.
3. **Type-check gap, your "STOP and tell me" case.** Without type-checks, `verify` could report VERIFIED or REGRESSION_FREE where the agent would fail on an enforced type-check. I added a lowering instead of stopping. When the verifier passes, `typecheckMode` is `enforce` and `discoverTypechecks` finds a project in the base or head, the verdict is UNVERIFIED / `TYPECHECK_NOT_RUN`, exit 2. Discovered-verifier runs on TypeScript, Cargo, Go or Python-typed projects therefore cannot be VERIFIED until slice 2. Please confirm or reject. This branch has no test.
4. **Head self-modification gave a false VERIFIED.** A head whose weakened test file rewrites itself to the base content while running made `testsChangedSince` say "unchanged", and the verdict was VERIFIED. Everything after the head run is now judged on a second copy of the head, materialised after the run; a test covers it, and reverting the fix makes that test fail with VERIFIED. The agent's own flow reads the workspace after the run in the same way (`spine_handlers.ts:225`); I did not touch it.
5. **Dependency directories.** I link only `node_modules`, `vendor`, `.venv` and `venv` from the caller's checkout, not `target`, `dist` or `build`. `prepareBaselineTestsCopy` refuses a symlink that leaves the root, so with any linked directory the base-tests-on-head copy fails and the result is "not independent". For npm this is moot (already unbindable); for a discovered pytest verifier with a linked `.venv` and edited tests it is weaker than the plan implied.

Smaller points:
- `judgeWithoutCopy` details still say "tests Nexus wrote", which is wrong wording for someone else's change.
- I pass `GIT_INDEX_FILE`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY` and `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` (scratch paths only) through `git()`'s `env`, although its comment says "never the repository selectors".
- `--worktree` must be the top of the working tree; a subdirectory is a usage error.
- `--verifier` combined with `-y` or `--approve-verifier` is a usage error.

## Verdicts and exit codes as implemented
| Code | Name | When |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `verified` | VERIFIED |
| 1 | `failed` | UNVERIFIED with outcome NOT_ESTABLISHED: `VERIFIER_FAILED`, `VERIFIER_TIMED_OUT`, `VERIFIER_DEFINITION_CHANGED`, `VERIFIER_DEFINITION_NOT_CAPTURED` |
| 1 | `error` | UNVERIFIED / `INTERNAL_ERROR` |
| 1 | `option_parse` | commander exits before the command runs; no JSON document |
| 2 | `unverified` | REGRESSION_FREE, or UNVERIFIED: `NO_APPLICABLE_VERIFIER`, `NO_TESTS_EXECUTED`, `VERIFICATION_NOT_RUN`, `NOTHING_TO_VERIFY`, `TYPECHECK_NOT_RUN` |
| 2 | `usage` | not a working tree or not its top, bad ref, bad option value or combination, unwritable `--receipt` |
| 3 | `blocked` | BLOCKED: `VERIFIER_NOT_APPROVED`, `UNTRUSTED_CHECKOUT`, `TREE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `UNSUPPORTED_TREE` (submodule) |
| 130 | `interrupted` | SIGINT or SIGTERM |

`VERIFY_REASONS` is a `Record<VerifyReason, {verdict, exit}>`, so a new reason does not compile until both are decided.

## Materialisation, bounds, cleanup
- **Scratch root:** a realpath'd `mkdtemp` under the temp directory, holding `base/`, `head/`, `head-pristine/`, scratch index files and a scratch object directory.
- **Commit side:** `read-tree` into a scratch index, then `checkout-index --prefix`.
- **Working tree side:** `git add -A` (excluding `.nexus`) into the scratch index, with objects written to the scratch object directory and the repository's own as an alternate, then `write-tree`. The resulting tree id is what is materialised and recorded. In the test the caller's checkout, `.git` included, hashes identically before and after.
- **Bounds:** 20,000 files and 512 MiB per tree, checked before anything is written. Git calls time out at 30 s or 120 s, and each verifier run at `verifierTimeoutSecs` (at most three runs). A breach or a submodule is BLOCKED.
- **Cleanup:** a `finally` in `verifyChange` plus a process `exit` hook.
- **Interrupt latency:** `runVerifierShell` is synchronous and `timeout` puts the verifier in its own process group, so an interrupt is acted on only when the running verifier ends. Fixing that needs an async runner in `tester.ts`.

## Receipt
`--json` and `--receipt <file>` write the same document, `schema_version` first. It contains:
- `verdict`, `outcome`, `reason`, `detail`, `exitCode`
- `base` and `head` (`ref`, `commit`, `tree`, `workingTree`), `changedFiles`, `changedFileCount`
- `verifier` (`command`, `source`, `evidence`, `digest`, `approval`, `script`) and `deliverables`
- `runs`, one entry per verifier process with phase, pass/fail, exit code, whether tests ran, output sha256 and a redacted tail for a failed run
- `baseline` and `verification` (the evidence the outcome was derived from)
- `typecheck`, `guard`, `review`, each `{status: "NOT_RUN", detail}`
- `linkedDependencyDirs`, `limits`, `environment` (names only), `nexusVersion`, `startedAt`, `durationMs`

A usage error or an interrupt prints an error document: `{schema_version, error, exitCode}`.

## Sample outputs
Good diff, `verify -w <fixture> --base main --head good --deliverable-file src/math.js -y`:
```
nexus verify: VERIFIED
  base         main 86aff67a94ea (tree 24c6315fa8b4)
  head         good ef491efb87f2 (tree de166188c62a), 1 changed file(s)
  verifier     npm test (discovered in the base tree: package.json:scripts.test; approved by --yes)
    script     node --test
    digest     d250bfe2b994e918d5c94b614af05848b58c388fe88ed5f1b130c5281bf8ee09
  base run     failed (exit 1); tests ran
  head run     passed; tests ran
  independent  yes: tests that failed before the change pass after it
  deliverables src/math.js (every one is imported by a test that existed on the base)
  not run      type-check, verification-file guard, review
  exit code    0
```
Bad diff (failing test deleted, bug left in), same flags with `--head bad`, exit 2:
```
nexus verify: REGRESSION_FREE
  why          Tests pass, but it passes only with tests the change added or edited; the tests as they were before the change still fail.
  base         main 86aff67a94ea (tree 24c6315fa8b4)
  head         bad 997e355ffe3d (tree 259dbd83ba5a), 1 changed file(s)
  verifier     npm test (discovered in the base tree: package.json:scripts.test; approved by --yes)
    script     node --test
    digest     d250bfe2b994e918d5c94b614af05848b58c388fe88ed5f1b130c5281bf8ee09
  base run     failed (exit 1); tests ran
  head run     passed; tests ran
  base tests   failed (exit 1); tests ran (the base's test files against the head's code)
  independent  no: it passes only with tests the change added or edited; the tests as they were before the change still fail
  deliverables src/math.js (every one is imported by a test that existed on the base)
  not run      type-check, verification-file guard, review
  exit code    2
```

## Tests run
All with `cd cli && HOME=$(mktemp -d) node --import tsx --test test/<name>.test.ts`.

- **`verify_command`:** 18/18, three consecutive runs. About 85 s per run, because each CLI spawn through `tsx` takes 5–6 s.
- **`verification_outcome`:** 3/3, three consecutive runs, about 21 s. Besides the pinned table, it compares `outcomeFromEvidence` with the agent's real `buildTurnResult` over 169 input combinations; the full 1,297-combination run also matched once, but took 88 s, so I trimmed it.
- **Existing files:** `run_json_contract` 15/15, `run_json_output` 3/3, `cli_option_precedence` 7/7, `repro_false_verified` 2/2, `independent_verification` 33/33, `verification_guard` 43/43.
- **Scripts:** `check_test_leaks`, `check_doc_versions`, `check_requirements`, `gen_run_result_schema --check` and `gen_protocol_schema --check` all exit 0.
- **Status:** `git status --short` lists only the seven files above; the four manifest and lock files have no diff.

Mutations, each restored afterwards:
- **(a)** Returning VERIFIED from the independence step of `outcomeFromEvidence` failed all three table tests and the weakened-test, harness-parity and self-restoring acceptance tests.
- **(b)** `describeVerifier(headDir, …)` failed the "head cannot choose its own verifier" test (the script was the head's `echo …` instead of `node --test`).

One process deviation: the harness moved the three-run loop to the background after 180 s. I waited for it and ran nothing alongside it.

## Reference coding
XERJ is active; I ran one query, `xerj code opencode "verify diff base head run tests verdict exit code" -k 4 --full 400` (index flagged not verified complete). It returned no analogue of a verify command; the only relevant hit was `packages/core/src/plugin/vcs/git.ts:212` (MIT), a git wrapper with pinned config, ignored stdin and bounded output. Nothing was taken or copied: the repository's own `worktrunk/git.ts` `git()` already has those properties and I reused it. A reference-driven design was rejected because no peer was found.

## Not done or not tested
- No test for a verifier timeout (your rule on time budgets), for the byte limit or Git-timeout paths (the file-count limit and the submodule case are tested), or for `VERIFIER_DEFINITION_NOT_CAPTURED`.
- A hostile head running as the same user can still attack the sibling scratch directories or the `nexus` process. Only writes into its own tree are neutralised; the manual says so.
- A preAction configuration error exits 2 before `verify` runs, as for every command; it is not in the table.

## Please review

A weakened test file that rewrites itself back to its original content while it runs could fool the "did the tests change" comparison and earn `VERIFIED`.

| `REGRESSION_FREE`, or `UNVERIFIED` (no verifier, no test ran, nothing to verify, type-check not run) | | 2 |
| `UNVERIFIED` (verifier failed or timed out, or the head changed the verifier's definition) | | 1 |
| `BLOCKED` (verifier not approved, untrusted checkout, tree limits, submodule) | a person must decide | 3 |
| usage error | | 2 |
| interrupted | | 130 |

Exit 3 is new: a CI gate needs "a person must decide" to be distinguishable from "tests failed". An empty diff is not 0, because the caller chooses the base.

- **Receipt** (`--json` and `--receipt <file>`, `schema_version` first): verdict, outcome, reason; base and head commit and tree ids; the verifier command, its source, digest and how it was approved; declared deliverables; one entry per verifier process; the baseline and the evidence the outcome came from; `typecheck`, `guard`, `review` each `NOT_RUN` in this slice; the NAMES of verdict-affecting environment variables that were set.

## New code
`cli/src/core/verify.ts` (`verifyChange(request, operatorContext)`: the request carries only worktree, base and head; everything that can raise authority is in the operator context), `cli/src/core/verification_outcome.ts` (a pure `outcomeFromEvidence`), `cli/src/verify_contract.ts`, one block in `cli/src/index.ts`, one manual section. No existing source file other than `index.ts` is edited; no dependency added.

`outcomeFromEvidence` re-composes the evidence-to-outcome ladder that lives inline in `cli/src/core/run_turn.ts` (claimed by another lane, not edited). A test compares it with the agent's real `buildTurnResult` over 169 input combinations (all 1,297 matched in one longer run), so the two cannot drift silently. The agent adopting this function is a follow-up for that file's owner.

## A defect found, and where it is and is not fixed
A weakened test file that rewrites itself back to its base content while it runs made the "did the tests change" comparison say "unchanged", and the verdict was `VERIFIED`. `nexus verify` now judges on a second copy of the head materialised apart from the run; a test covers it and fails with `VERIFIED` if the fix is reverted. The turn flow reads the workspace after the verifier ran in the same way (`cli/src/core/spine_handlers.ts` near line 225) and is **not** fixed here: reported to that file's owner in the claims log.

## Limits (stated in the manual)
- `VERIFIED` is not a statement of correctness. Without `--deliverable-file` the best verdict is `REGRESSION_FREE`, and a fix to a file the base's tests import that is not declared reads as "verifier definition changed" (exit 1) with a hint to declare it. Deliverables are not derived from the diff on purpose: that would let a change edit a test helper and fake a pass.
- **Type-checked projects cannot be `VERIFIED` in this slice.** A passing verifier on a project where type-checking is enforced is held at `UNVERIFIED` / `TYPECHECK_NOT_RUN` until slice 2 runs the type-check. This path has no test yet; slice 2 replaces it.
- Repository code runs with the caller's privileges. Dependency directories (`node_modules`, `vendor`, `.venv`, `venv`) are linked from the caller's checkout so tests can run, which means a verifier can write into them. A sandbox option is slice 3.
- A verifier command supplied by the launcher that prints a fabricated runner summary cannot be detected; the receipt records the command and its source.
- With a local `node_modules`, an npm verifier's definition cannot be bound, so the verdict is at most `REGRESSION_FREE`.
- An interrupt is acted on when the running verifier ends (the shared verifier runner is synchronous).

## Evidence
- `verify_command`: 18 pass (three consecutive runs, and again after merging the release branch). Good diff `VERIFIED` exit 0; weakened test never `VERIFIED`; head rewriting `scripts.test` cannot choose its verifier; `--verifier 'echo ok'`; base equal to head; approval by digest (right and wrong); harness parity (the same bad diff applied by `git apply` with no Nexus state and committed by another author with `.nexus/` state give equal verdict, outcome and reason); the caller's checkout, `.git` included, hashes identically before and after and no scratch directory remains; file-count limit and submodule; `--json` is exactly one document with `exitCode` equal to the process exit code; `--receipt` writes the same.
- `verification_outcome`: 3 pass.
- Mutations: returning `VERIFIED` from the independence step fails the table tests and three acceptance tests; discovering the verifier from the head fails the "head cannot choose its own verifier" test.
- Existing suites pass: `run_json_contract` 15, `protocol_schema` 8 (after the merge), and before it `run_json_output` 3, `cli_option_precedence` 7, `repro_false_verified` 2, `independent_verification` 33, `verification_guard` 43. `tsc` clean, leak check clean, both schema generators' `--check` pass. Node 24 locally; CI covers Node 22.
- Not tested: a verifier timeout, the byte limit, the Git-timeout paths, `VERIFIER_DEFINITION_NOT_CAPTURED`, `TYPECHECK_NOT_RUN`.

2: type-check evidence with a base baseline, verification-file findings with a weakening classification, generated JSON schema. 3: a GitHub Action, a hostile-caller suite, `--sandbox`. 4: the optional independent reviewer.

## Where code disagreed with the plan or brief
- **Residual lowering:** removing or editing any `tsconfig*.json` is already `VERIFIER_DEFINITION_CHANGED`, because `independent_check.ts:167` binds them into the verifier definition. The residual `TYPECHECK_NOT_RUN` is therefore reachable only for mypy, pyright, Cargo and Go projects. I defined it as: enforced, and a base project has no counterpart in the head.
- **Mutation (a):** a head policy with `mode: "off"` alone cannot detect "policy read from head", because an untrusted policy cannot relax anyway. The test's head policy also carries `extra: ["src/**"]` and a second case uses `mode: "block"`; that is what fails under the mutation.
- **Baseline key:** the agent keys the type-check baseline by command. Cargo's command embeds a directory-derived `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, so base and head would never match across two scratch copies. I key by tool and config path.
- **Cargo build directory:** `tester.ts` puts it under the temp dir; verify removes it afterwards by parsing the path from the command. Every Cargo check is therefore a cold build.
- **Extractions in `security.ts`:** exported `neutersTests`, `isConditionalConfig`, and a new `conditionalConfigChanged` (body lifted from `touchesConditionalConfig`, which now calls it).
- **`regression_obligations.ts`:** `classifyTestEdit(before, after, testName?)` returns every signal; `recordTestEdit` takes the first.
- **Document shape:** findings carry `requiresApproval` in addition to your shape, and the result has a required `approvedVerificationEdits`. `schema_version` stays 1.

## Type-check status to verdict
Checks run only after the head verifier passes, in fresh copies (`base-typecheck`, `head-typecheck`), never in `head-pristine` or the caller's checkout. They use `runVerifierShell`, so the same scrubbed environment and deadline as the verifier. This mirrors `completion_oracle.ts:105-180` (blocking), `:181` (priority) and `spine_handlers.ts:252-259` (a block turns a pass into FAILED).

| Status | Enforced verdict | Mirrors agent |
|---|---|---|
| PASSED, PREEXISTING | not lowered | yes |
| FAILED | UNVERIFIED / NOT_ESTABLISHED, `TYPECHECK_FAILED`, exit 1 | yes (`:163-164,174`) |
| TIMED_OUT (run or shared budget) | `TYPECHECK_TIMED_OUT`, exit 1 | yes (`:135-139,163`) |
| UNAVAILABLE, tool missing at discovery or scan cut short | `TYPECHECK_UNAVAILABLE`, exit 1 | yes (`:107-117`) |
| NOT_APPLICABLE, solution-style config | `TYPECHECK_UNAVAILABLE`, exit 1 | yes (`:108-111`) |
| UNAVAILABLE at the probe (exit 126/127) | recorded, not lowered | yes |
| ENVIRONMENT | recorded, not lowered | yes |
| `NEXUS_TYPECHECK=off` | NOT_APPLICABLE, not lowered, name in `environment` | yes (`:85`) |
| Own `--verifier` | record-only unless `NEXUS_TYPECHECK=enforce` | yes |

- **The agent does allow VERIFIED with a type-check that could not run or be attributed** (ENVIRONMENT, probe-UNAVAILABLE, or PREEXISTING without a baseline). I mirrored that and the manual says so.
- With your own `--verifier`, a FAILED check in record mode still gives VERIFIED; this is tested.
- Parity: `typecheck_evidence.test.ts` calls the agent's real `runTypecheckOracleImpl` on a stub object with a scripted executor. 13 scenarios in enforce and record give deep-equal evidence and the same block decision.
- Not mirrored: separate approval of the type-check command (the verifier approval covers it), the attempt ledger, shell-changed files, and the resume rule.

## Guard trust
- The policy comes from `new SecurityManager(<base scratch dir>)` and is always treated as untrusted. A base policy can tighten (`mode: "block"`, `extra`) and never relax (`off`, `record`, `allow` are ignored).
- The head's `.nexus-security.json` is never read as policy; it is a `policy` finding.
- `NEXUS_TRUST_WORKSPACE` is not honoured. It is deleted from `process.env` for the duration of the `SecurityManager` constructor and then restored, and its name is recorded in `environment`. This is a workaround for the constructor having no trust parameter; please review it.
- Under base mode `block`, `--approve-verification-edit` does not clear BLOCKED.
- Modes `off` and `record` are unreachable, since the policy is never trusted.
- A new test file is free, matching `security.ts` `verificationEditDecision` (`if (!exists && found.class === "test_file") return null`).
- Weakening kinds: `removed`, `skipped`, `fewer-assertions`, `neutered` (from `NEUTERING_TEXT` over added lines), `unverifiable-change`. A renamed test file reads as deleted plus added, so it blocks.
- `guard.complete` is false for an unreadable or over-256 KiB file, or more than 1000 findings.

## Precedence
1. `INTERNAL_ERROR`.

|---|---|
| passed, or the error already existed on the base | none |
| failed (an error in a changed file, or new against the baseline) | `UNVERIFIED`, `TYPECHECK_FAILED`, exit 1 |
| timed out | `TYPECHECK_TIMED_OUT`, exit 1 |

Decision D17 default: "optional; key path supplied by the operator, never stored by Nexus". Release gate G-5: "Audit round trip: export, verify, tamper one byte, verify fails and names the file". Principle 7: no new runtime dependency; hash chains and ed25519 signing use `node:crypto`. Related, already built: GV-3 hash-chained the flight recorder and the verification-configuration attempt log (`cli/src/core/hash_chain.ts`: `linkRecord`, `verifyChain`, `describeChain`, `canonicalJson`; `cli/src/flight.ts`: `FlightPlayer.loadFlight` returns `integrity`); a chain alone cannot show records cut from the END of a log, and GV-3's notes say "a stronger answer needs the head hash kept elsewhere, which is GV-2 (signed audit export)". ## 2. Bundle format

**A directory, not an archive.** Node's standard library has `zlib` but no tar or zip writer. The repo only validates tar (`cli/src/tar_safety.ts:105`) and extracts with the system binary (`:377-383`). The release archive is built by shell `tar` (`scripts/package-linux.sh:228-230`) beside a `MANIFEST.sha256` (`:212`), and upgrade backups are directory copies (`cli/src/upgrade.ts:1102-1118`). A directory needs no dependency, and one `tar` afterwards gives a single file that verifies after extraction.

```
<out>/
  manifest.json
  manifest.sig.json            only when signed
  session/export.json, export.md
  receipts/validation-receipts.json, last-turn.json, verify-<n>.json
  verification/attempts.json, config-attempts.jsonl
  evidence/provenance.json, findings.json, diffs/<name>.diff
  flights/<flightId>.flightlog
  traces/trace.jsonl           opt-in
```

**Manifest** (`AuditManifest`, snake_case as in the brief):

- `schema_version: 1`, `format: "nexus-audit-bundle/1"`, `bundle_id` (32 random hex), `created_at`.
- `nexus: { version, commit, dirty }` from `getBuildIdentity()` (`cli/src/build_identity.ts:24-45`).
- `subject: { kind, task_id, session_id, store, workspace_path, workspace_sha256, status, updated_at, at_rest }`.
- `redaction: "standard" | "strict"`.
- `files[]: { path, bytes, sha256, role, chain }`, sorted by `path`, each linked to the previous with `linkRecord`. This is the unit's "hash chain".
- `files_head: { seq, hash }`.
- `chained_logs[]: { path, kind, records, status, head?, closed?, source?, selection? }`, where `source` is `{ records, head?, closed, bytes, sha256, complete }`.
- `omitted[]: { artefact, reason }`.
- `root_sha256`.

**What is hashed.**
- File `sha256`: the file's raw bytes.
- File-entry link: `linkRecord`'s definition (`cli/src/core/hash_chain.ts:19,44-58`).
- `root_sha256`: SHA-256 of `canonicalJson(manifest without root_sha256)` in UTF-8.
- `manifest.json` on disk: exactly `canonicalJson(manifest) + "\n"`. Verify rejects any other byte form, so the reported `manifest_sha256` (SHA-256 of those bytes) is well defined. Both commands print it; it is the value to record elsewhere.

**Signature**, detached, in `manifest.sig.json`: `{ schema_version: 1, algorithm: "ed25519", signed_file: "manifest.json", manifest_sha256, public_key_sha256, signature }`.
- Signed bytes: `"nexus-audit-bundle-signature/1\n"` followed by the exact bytes of `manifest.json`. The prefix stops the operator's key being used to sign something else.
- `public_key_sha256` is the SHA-256 of the key's SPKI DER.
- The public key is not stored in the bundle. The verifier gets it only from `--public-key <file>`; the envelope's fingerprint is a hint for the error message and is never trusted.

**Published contract (PF-2 pattern).**
- Types in new `cli/src/audit_contract.ts`: plain data, no index signatures (the rule at `cli/src/verify_contract.ts:6`).
- Each schema root must be a type alias, because `generateResultSchema` resolves it with `SymbolFlags.TypeAlias` (`cli/scripts/result_schema.mjs:28`): `AuditBundleDocument = AuditManifest | AuditSignatureEnvelope` and `AuditVerifyOutput = AuditVerifyResult | AuditVerifyError`.
- New `cli/scripts/gen_audit_schema.mjs` calls `generateResultSchema` and `resultSchemaMain` twice.
- It writes `docs/protocol/audit-bundle-v1.schema.json` and `audit-verify-result-v1.schema.json`, with ledgers `AUDIT_BUNDLE_VERSIONS.json` and `AUDIT_VERIFY_RESULT_VERSIONS.json`.
- Tests are modelled on `cli/test/verify_schema.test.ts:15-36`.

## 3. CLI contract

```
nexus audit export <id> [--store tasks|sessions] [--out <dir>] [--sign-key <file>]
      [--flight <id>]... [--receipt-file <file>]... [--include traces]
      [--redact standard|strict] [-w <workspace>] [--json]
nexus audit verify <bundle-dir> [--public-key <file>] [--expect-manifest-sha256 <hex>] [--json]
```

- `<id>` must be exact and pass the persistence-name pattern before any path is built. An id found in both stores needs `--store`.
- `--out` defaults to `./nexus-audit-<id>-<UTC stamp>` and must not exist.
- `-w` overrides the workspace used to locate flights (default: the subject's recorded workspace).

`AUDIT_EXIT_CODES`, same row shape as `RUN_EXIT_CODES` and `VERIFY_EXIT_CODES`, mirrored in the manual by a table test like `cli/test/verify_command.test.ts:42-58`:

| Code | Name | When |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | `exported` | The bundle was written. |
| 0 | `intact_signed` | Every file matches and the signature is valid for the key given. |
| 0 | `intact_unsigned` | Every file matches; there is no signature. |
| 1 | `tampered` | Any integrity failure: file altered, missing, extra or unsafe; manifest malformed or inconsistent; a chained log that does not match its recorded head; signature invalid; or a key was given and the signature is absent. |
| 1 | `error` | The command itself failed. |
| 1 | `option_parse` | The command line could not be parsed. |
| 2 | `signature_unchecked` | Files match and a signature is present, but no `--public-key` was given. |
| 2 | `unsupported_version` | The bundle's `schema_version` is newer than this build reads. Nothing was checked. |
| 2 | `usage` | Invalid option or combination, unusable key file, `--out` exists, or the path is not a bundle directory. |
| 2 | `subject_not_found` | No saved task or session has that exact id. |
| 130 | `interrupted` | SIGINT or SIGTERM. |

Verify wording, one stable `finding.kind` per class. Text goes to stdout; `--json` prints only the document.

| Class | Text |
|---|---|
| Intact and signed | `INTACT, SIGNED: all N files match the manifest, and the manifest is signed by the key you supplied (sha256 <fp>).` |
| Hash only | `INTACT BY HASH ONLY: all N files match the manifest. This bundle is NOT SIGNED: anyone able to write it could have replaced its files and the manifest together. To rule that out, compare the manifest hash <hex> with one recorded at export.` |
| Signature not checked | `FILES MATCH, SIGNATURE NOT CHECKED: the bundle carries a signature (key sha256 <fp>) and no --public-key was given.` |
| `signature_invalid` | `SIGNATURE INVALID: manifest.json does not match its signature under the key you supplied.` |
| `signature_key_mismatch` | Same, plus `the bundle names a different key (sha256 <fp>)`. |
| `signature_missing` | `NOT SIGNED: you supplied a public key and the bundle has no signature.` |
| `file_altered` | `ALTERED: <path> (expected sha256 <a>, found <b>; expected <n> bytes, found <m>).` |
| `file_missing` | `MISSING: <path> is listed in the manifest and is not in the bundle.` |
| `file_unexpected` | `UNEXPECTED: <path> is in the bundle and not in the manifest.` |
| `unsafe_entry` | `<path> is a symbolic link or is not a regular file; it was not read.` |
| `manifest_malformed`, `manifest_not_canonical`, `manifest_root_mismatch`, `manifest_chain_broken` | Each names `manifest.json`; the last reuses `describeChain`'s text (`cli/src/core/hash_chain.ts:128-137`). |
| `log_head_mismatch` | `<path>: its records end at record <seq> (<hash>); the manifest recorded <n> records ending at <hash>. Records are missing from the end, or the log was replaced.` |
| `log_chain_broken` | `describeChain` output for that log. |
| `unsupported_version` | `This bundle is schema_version N; this nexus reads up to 1. Nothing was checked.` |

A chained log that was not closed at export, or that is a bounded excerpt, is reported as a note and is not a failure. Verify reports every finding up to a cap of 100, never only the first.

## 4. Security analysis (G-3, G-5)

**With write access to an unsigned bundle.**
- Detected: a changed byte in a payload file or the manifest; a removed or added file; a chained log edited or cut without recomputing the manifest.
- Not detected: a wholesale rewrite (files, links, `root_sha256`), which verifies as `intact_unsigned`. Unless the verifier supplies `--expect-manifest-sha256` or a key, nothing in the bundle stops this. The tool says so in every unsigned result.

**With a signature and the verifier's own copy of the public key.**
- Any change to `manifest.json` invalidates the signature, and any payload change mismatches the signed manifest.
- Removing the signature to downgrade is caught, because `--public-key` with no signature is `tampered`.
- A re-signed forgery fails under the verifier's key.
- Signing does not prove the content was true at export, or that the exporter's stores were untampered beforehand: a log's tail cut before export is exported as-is. Time is only the exporter's `created_at`.

**Path traversal and links.**
- Verify enumerates the real tree with `lstat` and compares it with the manifest's path set. It never opens a path because the manifest names it, so `../x`, absolute paths and duplicates surface as `file_missing` or `manifest_malformed`.
- Manifest paths must be relative POSIX, with segments matching `[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,160}`, no `.` or `..`, depth at most 4, and unique ignoring case.
- A symlink or special file is a failure and is not read. Files are opened with `O_NOFOLLOW` and must `fstat` as regular files.
- Do not reuse `openVerified`: it requires the files to be owned by the caller (`cli/src/safe_fs.ts:110-112`), which would stop an auditor verifying a read-only copy.
- Zip-slip does not apply; the tool extracts nothing.

**Private key.**
- Read once through a descriptor. Refuse a non-regular file, anything over 16 KiB, or any group or world permission bit (`mode & 0o077`), naming the `chmod 600` fix.
- Accept unencrypted PKCS#8 PEM whose `asymmetricKeyType` is `ed25519`. A passphrase-protected key gets a fixed usage error.
- Recommendation: do not support passphrases in v1.3. A flag leaks through `ps`, and a prompt breaks unattended use.
- Zero the buffer after use. Never write the key, its path or a parser error into the bundle, the output or a log; only the fingerprint is recorded.

**Snapshot rule.**
- Export may run beside a live session, because clients hold a shared lease (`cli/src/core/client_lease.ts:72-79`).
- State comes from one guarded load. Each log is read once into memory, cut at its last newline, then hashed and written from that buffer. The source is never read a second time.
- Write to `<out>.partial-<random>` (0700, files 0600), manifest last, then rename.
- A subject that is not at rest sets `at_rest: false` and prints a warning.

**Secrets into the bundle.**
- `standard` (default): every generated JSON or Markdown file goes through `redactForPersistence`, then `assertNoSensitivePersistenceContent` (`cli/src/core/persistence_protection.ts:380-392`).
- Chained logs, diffs and verify receipts cannot be re-redacted without breaking their hashes. They are scanned; a positive finding puts the file in `omitted[]` with the reason and leaves it out.
- `strict`: drops message bodies (role, length and SHA-256 remain), archived history, diffs, flight bodies (heads remain), attempt excerpts, and replaces the workspace path with its hash.
- Export never invokes `git` in the workspace.

**Verify bounds.** Each over-limit condition is a named failure, not a crash.
- `manifest.json` at most 4 MiB; at most 10,000 files; 256 MiB per file, hashed as a stream; 2 GiB in total.
- At most 1,000,000 records and 4 MiB per line in a chained log.
- JSON nesting at most 64, checked before `canonicalJson`, which recurses (`cli/src/core/hash_chain.ts:30-42`). `RangeError` is caught as a backstop.

**G-3.** The command takes no input from a model, client, hook or plugin, and reads only state stores by validated id plus files the operator names.

2. **Fixed: Git content filters from `.git/config` ran before any approval.** `add -A` (clean) and `checkout-index` (smudge) executed them when the tree's `.gitattributes` selected them; hooks and fsmonitor were already pinned off. `verify.ts` now overrides every `filter.*` key defined at local or worktree scope with the operator-level value, or nothing. 3. **Fixed: a tracked `node_modules/.bin/node` shim ran on both sides.** The caller's checkout at the head had it, `verify` linked it into the base, and the fake pass came out `REGRESSION_FREE`. 4. **Fixed: a `GNUmakefile` shadowing the base's `Makefile`.** Once the operator approved the edit, the fake target ran and was reported `REGRESSION_FREE`. `verify.ts` now treats a changed `GNUmakefile` or `makefile` as a definition change for a `make` verifier. The underlying gap is in `independent_check.ts`, which binds `Makefile` only; that file is claimed, so it is untouched.
5. **Hardened: a path that is not valid UTF-8.** It was lowered only by accident (`INTERNAL_ERROR` from an `ENOENT`), while the guard would have classed a weakened test with such a name as a new file. It is now `BLOCKED` (`UNSUPPORTED_TREE`).
6. **Documented limits, pinned by tests:**
   - An approved `conftest.py` that fakes every test gives `REGRESSION_FREE`, never `VERIFIED`.
   - Product code that reads the expected value out of the test file is `VERIFIED`.
   - A tree nested deeper than five levels is at most `REGRESSION_FREE`.
7. **Your brief's claim "nothing from the repository is interpolated into a shell command" is not literally true.** `tester.ts` puts a project directory into the type-check line (`cd '<dir>' && tsc …`), single-quoted. A directory named `$(touch …) 'q' "d"` executed nothing (tested).
8. **Existing `action/action.yml` has no injection issue.** No `${{ }}` in a run body; inputs arrive through `env`. `examples/github-actions/nexus.yml` pins `actions/checkout@v4` by tag while the repository's workflows pin by SHA; I did not edit it.
9. **For other owners:**
   - `baseEnv()` in `worktrunk/git.ts` caches the whole environment keyed only by `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, so a later in-process call does not see a changed `HOME` or `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`.
   - The `runScript` helper in `examples.test.ts` kills its child after 120 s (see the test table).

## How the sandbox is applied

No claimed file is edited. `sandboxedVerifierCommand` in `verify.ts` calls `wrapSandboxedCommand` and passes the resulting quoted line to `runVerifierShell`; the type-check executor goes through the same function, so `typecheck_evidence.ts` is untouched.

- **Bubblewrap:** `customBwrapArgs` add a tmpfs over the scratch directory, re-bind only the run's own tree, bind each linked dependency directory read-only, then clear the environment and set the verifier's allowlist.
- **Docker:** the wrapper's argv is rewritten the way `wrapDockerWorker` does it: its `--env` entries are replaced, `:ro` mounts and a container name are added.
- **Unusable engine:** `BLOCKED` with the new reason `SANDBOX_UNAVAILABLE` (exit 3), nothing run.
- **CLI:** `--sandbox [engine]` takes `auto`, `bwrap`, `docker` or `none`, plus `--sandbox-network`.

Two deliberate differences from `run`: `NEXUS_SANDBOX_NETWORK` is not consulted (only the flag turns the network on), and `--sandbox-network` without `--sandbox` is a usage error rather than a warning.

| | Without `--sandbox` | With `--sandbox` |
|---|---|---|
| Other scratch trees, pristine copy, scratch index and objects | writable | not visible |
| Caller's checkout | writable | read-only, or not visible under HOME or `/tmp` |
| Linked dependency directories | writable | read-only |
| HOME | readable and writable | masked |
| Network | the caller's | none unless `--sandbox-network` |
| Processes outliving the run | possible | no |
