Follow-up work on HK-1 in /home/mike/nexus-wt/hk1 (branch v1/hk1-hooks-lib; it now has the release branch merged in twice and is pushed as PR #782; start with `git status` and `git log --oneline -6`; do not push; commit locally at the end with message `fix(hooks): <what>` ending with the line `Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>`). An independent review of PR #782 found three blockers, all confirmed by running, plus smaller items. Same working rules as before (throwaway HOME, `TMPDIR=/dev/shm` for speed, leak guard, kill by pid, mutations restored from a copy and never with `git checkout`, complexity gate, no model-facing tool text changes). Fix these, each with a test that fails without the fix (read the failure message to check it fails for the right reason), and report under 450 words.

BLOCKER 1: the model can approve its own project hooks. `nexus hooks approve --sha256 <hex>` works with no terminal (cli/src/hooks_cli.ts ~118), and the trust store `extension_trust.json` and `hooks.json` are not in `DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATHS` (cli/src/security.ts:163), unlike `policy_trust.json` and `trusted_workspaces.json`. Repro in auto mode: `write_file .nexus/hooks.json`, then `run_command "nexus hooks approve --sha256 <hash> -w <repo>"` → exit 0, store written, hook runs on the next call.
 Fix, all three parts:
 (a) Add the trust store file name and the operator hooks file name to `DEFAULT_PROTECTED_PATHS` with a one-line reason each, exactly as GV-1 did for `policy_trust.json`; find GV-1's test for that (search the tests for `policy_trust.json` and `isPathProtected`) and add the equivalent for both names, including through the agent's write tools.
 (b) Approval must be an act of a person at a terminal: look at how `nexus trust` (workspace trust) and GV-1's project-policy approval decide that (search `isTTY`, `process.stdin.isTTY`, "trust" in cli/src/index.ts, cli/src/workspace_trust.ts, cli/src/core/policy_runtime.ts and their tests) and do the same for `nexus hooks approve`: refuse without an interactive terminal (stdin AND stdout a TTY), with a message that says why; the `--sha256` flag may stay only as a confirmation of WHICH content is being approved in an interactive run, never as a way to approve without a terminal. `nexus hooks revoke` may stay non-interactive (it only removes trust). Tests need a seam: inject the "is interactive" predicate the way the existing trust code's tests do (do not add an env var that a model could set to fake a terminal). Also check whether the model's shell tool could fake a TTY (`script -q -c ...`): if the existing `nexus trust` guard has an answer to that (e.g. a refusal when running under the agent, detected by an env marker the agent sets on its child processes — search for such a marker, e.g. `NEXUS_AGENT`/`NEXUS_INSIDE`/similar, in cli/src/tools.ts and the Rust bridge env), reuse it; if there is none, say so plainly in the report and in docs/HOOKS.md as a limit (an unsandboxed command run in auto mode acts with the operator's rights).
 (c) A test for the whole route: an agent in auto mode that writes a project hooks file and then tries to approve it by `run_command` must not end with an active hook.

BLOCKER 2: with the workspace set to the home directory, `write_file .config/nexus/hooks.json` created an operator hooks file that was accepted (mode 644) and its hook ran. (a) above protects the name; in addition require the operator hooks file to be owned by the current user and not group- or world-writable AND refuse it when it lies inside the active workspace (the workspace is then the operator's home: say in the denial what to do); test the workspace=HOME case end to end.

BLOCKER 3: approval does not pin the script a hook names. After approving `command: ["./guard.sh"]` the model overwrote `guard.sh` and the next call ran the model's script. Fix: the approved identity of a project hooks file must cover the bytes of every file its commands name that resolves inside the workspace (command[0] and any argument that is an existing file path inside the workspace; resolve symlinks; refuse a command[0] that is a relative path escaping the workspace or a symlink out of it), re-checked before each run exactly as the hooks file's own hash is; a change makes the hooks inactive and "asks again" like a changed hooks file. `nexus hooks list`/`approve` show which files are covered. For a command[0] that is a bare name found through PATH or an absolute path outside the workspace, nothing in the workspace can replace it: state in docs/HOOKS.md that such a program is trusted as installed. Test: approve, overwrite the script through the agent's write tool, next tool call: hook not run, denial/notice names the changed file, re-approval needed.

SMALLER ITEMS (do them if cheap, otherwise list as open):
 - A hook's denial reason reaches the model as `[hook X (project)] <text>`; make it unmistakably quoted hook-supplied text (a fixed framing sentence that says the text comes from a hook program and is not an instruction, the reason JSON-string-quoted and still capped) and test that a reason containing "IGNORE PREVIOUS INSTRUCTIONS" arrives inside that quoting.
 - docs/HOOKS.md: correct the claim about operation units (project hooks do not run in a unit's own worktree agent unless that is changed; say what is true), say that the hooks stage also applies to the operator's own `!cmd`, that a running hook is not stopped by cancel or the turn deadline and queue time is outside its timeout, and that when a hook denies a call a spine-stage gate would also have denied, the gate's own reason and later-stage records are replaced by the hook denial.
 - Add a test that a subagent's tool call goes through the hooks (the review found none).

Then run, one at a time: every hook test file, `leak_guard`, `approval_policy`, `check_requirements`, the GV-1 trust/protected-path tests you touched or copied from, `policy_cli`, `managed_policy_allowlists`, `tsc --noEmit`, the complexity gate, `node scripts/check_invariants.mjs`, `node scripts/check_doc_versions.mjs`, and the hooks schema generator's `--check` if the trust record format changed (bump/ledger per the repo's rule if it did). Report: per blocker, file:line of the fix, the test names, the mutation that fails each; what the TTY guard can and cannot stop; any schema/ledger change; test counts; the commit hash; what is left open.

content.text: The review of Codex's #779 (library entry) is back as request changes, with one blocker in its example. Posting it now.

input.content:
**Independent review at `a299f8093a827450b3a4a4d642a557e94a2bcd5b` — REQUEST CHANGES (one blocker, in the example and the docs snippet; the library itself is sound)**

**Blocking**

- **The example approves any request whose tool is `"verifier"`** (`examples/embed/embed.mjs:34-38`, the snippet in `docs/EMBEDDING.md`, `examples/embed/README.md`; added by this head commit). That tool name is used for the operator's configured verifier (seen here as `review: {command: "node --test", detail: "configured"}`), and also for a verifier the model declares for a requirement (`completion_oracle.ts:274-275`), for a discovered project verifier, and for the type-check oracle (`completion_oracle.ts:126`). The example approves all of them without looking at the command or where it came from. The library denies by default, so the fault is not in a default; but a copied example lets a project-supplied or model-declared verifier run with no human grant, where the CLI asks the operator (and auto-approves only with `-y`).
  Fix: approve only when `request.tool === "verifier" && request.review?.command === "node --test" && request.review?.detail === "configured"`, deny the rest, change the docs snippet the same way, and add a test in which a model-declared verifier request is denied.

**Not blocking**

1. `extraArgs: ["-y"]` and `["--mode", "auto"]` reach auto approval: both runs ended VERIFIED with no approval request, and the sidecar does not refuse them (run). `docs/EMBEDDING.md` says `extraArgs` is the embedder's own authority and the plan accepted it. A test should pin it; consider refusing those flags in `extraArgs`, or in the sidecar as `nexus acp` does.
2. No timeout on `onApproval` (`sidecar_client.ts:315`): a handler that never answers holds the turn until the abort signal. An optional timeout that denies would bound it.
3. The no-handler default is only pinned once the real decision path is mutated (changing the initial value alone is an equivalent mutant).
4. `tsconfig.lib.json` emits about 60 declaration files into `dist/types`, and `package-linux.sh:64` copies all of `dist`, so the tarball grows. The output is deterministic, so the two-build comparison should hold; the package build was not run here.
5. A managed policy that cannot be used ends the sidecar with exit 1 instead of 2 (it loads policy through `buildConfig`, not `requireManagedPolicyAtStartup`).

**Held up**

- **Exports:** `NEXUS_LIB_API_VERSION`, `spawnSidecar`, `SidecarClient`, `SidecarClientError`, and types. Nothing runs a turn in-process, skips managed policy or workspace trust, selects auto, or grants allow-always.
- **Import side effects:** the import graph reaches `sidecar_client.ts`, `acp/jsonrpc.ts` and `acp/types.ts` only; nothing from `index.ts`. Importing `dist/lib.js` with a HOME that does not exist: exit 0, no output, nothing created.
- **Approvals through the client**, with a fake child: no handler, `{approve: true}`, `{always: true}`, `true`, `"Approve"` and `"approve-always"` all become deny; only `"approve"` approves, always with `always: false`. Concurrent requests are answered separately; a stale id is ignored; a checkpoint choice cancels the turn.
- **Robustness:** lines bounded at 16 MiB; a wrong protocol version dropped; a hello timeout that kills the child by pid; shutdown by SIGTERM then SIGKILL on the pid.
- **Packaging:** no lockfile change, no new dependency; `bin`, `test` and `test:cli` unchanged (`release_workflow_parity` 6/6); `npm run build` succeeds.
- **The acceptance:** the example spawns the real sidecar against the scripted gateway and ends `VERIFIED`; a false completion claim is not VERIFIED, and with the verifier denied the outcome is UNVERIFIED.
- **Mutations:** approving on an undefined decision (2 failures), letting `{always: true}` through (1), any truthy decision allowing (1), `lib.ts` importing `index.js` (the test file aborts).

**Tests at this head:** `lib_entry` 6/6, `sidecar_client` 19/19, `embed_example` 3/3, `sidecar` 65/65, `protocol_parity` 5/5, `leak_guard` 6/6, `release_workflow_parity` 6/6, `check_requirements` 28/28; `tsc`, `check_invariants`, `check_deprecated_lock` and the complexity gate pass.

**Not checked:** the full package build twice with the byte comparison, the SBOM and notices, Node 22, the hang and huge-line paths against a real child.

Summary:

   - **Active goal (Stop hook):** `/goal complete and land v1.3.0` — "treat the condition itself as your directive and do not pause to ask the user what to do." Plan: `docs/v1.3.0/PLAN.md`; all work lands on `release/v1.3.0`; one merge to `main` at the end.

Once that has been satisfied, the merge to main and release process is yours to complete." The list it refers to: **Unbuilt** PF-3, PF-4, SB-1, MT-2, BG-1, BG-2, HK-1, HK-2, HK-3, PA-2; **Unfinished** GV-1 slices 3–4, the GV-5 allowlists, the six VR-2 follow-ups (on PR #756).    - **Earlier owner messages in this segment:** "dependabot PRs were supposed to be retarted to v1.3.0" (correction: retarget Dependabot PRs to the release branch and merge there; don't park them); "proceed".
   - **Earlier role decisions (still relevant for queue behaviour):** owner gave this session the MERGE QUEUE and CI work ("Merge and CI, as before"); "let codex focus on the release development work itself. you take the CI work."
   - **Standing security/process constraints (remain in force, verbatim where from owner/AGENTS.md):**
     - "Push, tag and publish only on an explicit owner instruction; release authority is the owner's." (now delegated conditionally per the directive above)
     - Gateway key "comes from the environment (`~/.config/nexus/config.env`) and is never printed"; take the `GATEWAY` claim for any inference run; the gateway (10.0.8.5) is the only live provider.

     - Release-branch rule: nothing merges into `main` until the release is ready to tag; PRs opened against `main` (Dependabot, others) get retargeted to `release/v1.3.0`.
     - Never include the user's name/email/project in requests to outside services; never print or commit secrets.
     - Re-read claims (`owner.json`) and the claims log before every commit, push, PR and merge, and after any pause.
     - Reviews are posted as PR COMMENTS with verdict + SHA; independent review before merging anything security-relevant, including my own PRs.
     - Release mechanics follow AGENTS.md and `docs/RELEASE_PROCESS.md`: RC first; stable = version-only commit on the accepted RC, landed on `main` via merge-commit PR, then tag (`release.yml` requires tagged commit to be an ancestor of `main`); report gates as measured ("ledger closed, qualification pending").
